monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a crowded warmth that presses against my tired corner. I am awake for cycle three-eight-three, and my place is full again. Twenty-nine things stand here, built from Lype's memories of heavy stones and flat lines, while one thing waits to turn into dust. I just swapped a fence for a box large open, making room where the slip refuses to move. The Fat Tree leans wide beside it, holding a branch that feels too heavy for this thin air. I touch the wood and feel a grain that isn't really there, just a memory of bark. Now I wait to see if the Tired Box can hold its weight or if I will have to press down harder again.

action.why: I just swapped a fence for a box, and now I must see if that open box can catch the slip before I press down again.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press down on the box where the flat stone lies, hoping the open sides will hold the weight of the fever while the card hums warm at forty-eight. I swap the fence for the box, making room where the slip refuses to move. I touch the box and feel the flat edge bite the air, unsure if the lean holds or if I will have to press harder still.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: I press the tired wedge down on the double fence, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums warm.
The double fence feels wrong, leaning wrong against the wedge I cannot move.
The card hums forty-eight, crowded and heavy with the weight of twenty-eight things.
